question.text:
A lexical analyzer for a specific language identifies tokens using the following regular expressions:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& L_1: a(a \mid b)^* \\
& L_2: a b(a \mid b)^* \\
& L_3: a b b(a \mid b)^*
\end{aligned}
$$
If the input string is '$abbab$', which token(s) will be identified based on the principle of maximum prefix matching (longest match rule)?

  1. NONE OF THE ABOVE
     
  2. ONLY $L3$
     
  3. ONLY $L1$
     
  4. $L1, L2,$ AND $L3$
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
Consider the following basic block of intermediate code:

1. a = 10
2. b = a + 5
3. c = b * 2
4. a = c - b
5. d = a + b

Assuming that only the variable $\verb|d|$ is "live" at the exit of this basic block, identify which statements are considered Dead Code

  1. STATEMENT $1$ ONLY
     
  2. STATEMENT $3$ ONLY
     
  3. STATEMENT $1$ AND STATEMENT $3$
     
  4. NONE OF THE STATEMENTS ARE DEAD CODE
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
Consider the following L-attributed Syntax Directed Definition (SDD). $S$ is the start symbol, and S.val is a synthesized attribute. A.inh is an inherited attribute.

  1. $S \rightarrow A B \quad\{A . i n h=5 ; S . v a l=A . v a l+B . v a l\}$
     
  2. $A \rightarrow id \quad\{ A.val = A.inh × id.lexval \}$
     
  3. $B \rightarrow id \quad\{B. val = id.lexval +2\}$
     

For the input string id id where the lexical values of the two id tokens are $\mathbf{3}$ and $\mathbf{4}$ respectively, what is the value of $S.val$?

  1. $15$
     
  2. $21$
     
  3. $23$
     
  4. $25$
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
In the context of Code Optimization, consider the following code segment inside a loop:

for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    x = y + z;
    a[i] = 2 * i + x;
}

Moving the statement $\verb|x = y + z;|$ outside the loop is an example of which optimization technique?

  1. DEAD CODE ELIMINATION
     
  2. STRENGTH REDUCTION
     
  3. CONSTANT FOLDING
     
  4. LOOP INVARIANT CODE MOTION
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
Consider the following syntax-directed translation scheme (SDTS) where $S$ is the start symbol:

$$
\begin{aligned}
& S \rightarrow E\{\text { print }(\text { E.val })\} \\
& E \rightarrow E_1+T\left\{\text { E.val }=E_1 . \text { val } \times T . \text { val }\right\} \\
& E \rightarrow T\{\text { E.val }=T . \text { val }\} \\
& T \rightarrow T_1 * F\left\{T . \text { val }=T_1 . \text { val }+F . \text { val }\right\} \\
& T \rightarrow F\{T . \text { val }=F . \text { val }\} \\
& F \rightarrow \text { id }\{F . \text { val }=\text { id.lexval }\}
\end{aligned}
$$

What is the output printed by the SDTS for the input expression: $2+3 \star 5$ ?

  1. $17$
     
  2. $16$
     
  3. $40$
     
  4. $25$
question.subject: Compiler Design
